questions.question: A frame of reference consists of:
options: A reference point and a chosen positive direction
An origin and a speed limit

questions.question: With the start as zero and east positive, the walker after 40 m east then 30 m west is at position:
A passenger in a moving taxi is stationary relative to the seat and moving relative to the road. This shows that:
options: The passenger is really moving and the seat's view is wrong
Motion is described relative to a chosen frame of reference — both descriptions are correct
Only the road can be a reference point
The taxi has two speeds at once in one frame

questions.question: In a declared frame, the sign of a position tells you:
options: How fast the object is moving
Which side of the reference point the object is on

questions.question: Distance and displacement are, respectively:
options: A scalar (path length) and a vector (change in position)

questions.question: For the 40 m east then 30 m west walk, the distance and displacement are:
One full lap of a 400 m track gives a displacement of:
options: Zero — the change in position is nothing

questions.question: Distance and the magnitude of displacement are equal only when:
options: The object returns to its start

questions.question: Average speed and average velocity are calculated as:
options: Speed from displacement; velocity from distance
Speed from distance over time; velocity from displacement over time

questions.question: For the walk (70 m distance, 10 m east displacement, 50 s), the average speed is:
The average velocity for the same walk is:
A runner completes a 400 m lap in 80 s. Average speed and average velocity are:

subtopics.title: The Full Method, the Classic Traps, and Where This Leads

questions.question: Displacement is computed from:
options: The sum of all path lengths
The endpoints only — final position minus initial position
The longest leg of the journey
The average of the leg lengths

questions.question: A walker rests for 10 s midway through a journey. For average speed, the time used is:
options: The walking time minus the rest
The total time, rest included — the clock does not pause

questions.question: An answer of '0,2 m/s' to a question asking for average velocity is incomplete because:
options: Velocity is a vector, so the direction must be stated
The magnitude is too small to report

questions.question: This vocabulary matters for later topics because:
options: Distance is the only quantity used in Grade 12
Acceleration, the equations of motion and momentum are all built on velocity and displacement, the vectors
Speed replaces velocity from Grade 11 onward

subtopics.title: Where Are You, Relative to What

questions.question: 'From the taxi rank, two streets up' illustrates that every position needs:
options: A reference point to measure from

questions.question: With the rank as zero and up-the-hill positive, the school one street down the hill has position:
The minus sign in a position like −10 m means:
options: The object is on the negative-direction side of the reference point
The object is below the ground

questions.question: Physics resolves the moving-taxi puzzle by:
options: Ruling that the road frame is the true one
Requiring you to declare a frame and stay loyal to it — both frames are legitimate

questions.question: In the two-instruments picture, the odometer and the pigeon measure, respectively:
options: Distance (every metre of the route) and displacement (straight line, start to finish)

questions.question: For the 40 m east, 30 m west walk, the odometer and pigeon readings are:
After a full lap of the track, 'the pigeon does not even take off' because:
options: Start and finish are the same point, so the displacement is zero
The lap was too fast to measure

questions.question: The gap between the odometer's 70 m and the pigeon's 10 m was created by:
options: Doubling back — the return leg grew the distance while shrinking the net change of position

questions.question: The 'odometer over time' and 'pigeon over time' divisions give:
The walker's two averages, 1,4 m/s and 0,2 m/s east, differ by a factor of seven because:
options: The stopwatch ran fast on one leg
Most of the walking undid earlier walking, so the net progress was small
The averages used different time values

questions.question: A delivery scooter zigzags all afternoon and ends near where it started. Its averages will show:
options: A small speed and a large velocity
A large speed and a tiny velocity

questions.question: When a question asks for velocity, the complete answer must include:
options: Both the speed and the velocity
The magnitude only, to two decimals
